method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Background only: names objectives A to C and says licensees and BCTS should consider the Implementation Policy; imposes nothing on a block.
Establishes the order's landscape units as the merged BEC units of Map #2, which are the units every old and old interior forest figure for a block's schedule is measured over.
sections.gapNote: Code reads the Map 2 units from DataBC's legal layer (orderUnits.ts, oldForest/units.ts); the ground screen shows the order extent.

sections.bearsOn: Establishes objectives A to D, objective C over Map #1 (natural disturbance sub-units) and A and B over Map #2 (merged BEC units).
sections.gapNote: Both maps' units are read from the legal layer by code (Compare: old forest and patch analysis). The order says "A through D" though D is contributions and alternatives rather than an objective.

sections.bearsOn: The objectives apply to all Crown land in the PG TSA except land under woodlot licences, TFLs or community forest licences, and replace the June 30, 2004 provincial non-spatial old growth order there.
sections.gapNote: Code removes non-Crown land, woodlots (W), community forests (K) and TFLs in prepareUnit (landBase.ts) and keeps First Nations woodland licences and research forests because the order does not name them. The 2022 letter of expectations says the order "does not automatically apply" to FNWLs and research forests either, and the ministry's COFA analysis left all area-based tenures out; a reviewer switch or a note would show the difference.

sections.bearsOn: The map that bounds objective C's natural disturbance sub-units.
sections.gapNote: Read as polygons from the legal layer for the patch analysis.

sections.bearsOn: The map that bounds the merged BEC units used for old and old interior forest.
sections.gapNote: Read as polygons from the legal layer (orderUnits.ts).

sections.bearsOn: Old forest must be maintained on the CFLB of each merged BEC unit at no less than the percentage in Tables 1 to 3, subject to section D; a block that harvests old forest draws that balance down.
sections.gapNote: Old forest module (oldForest/*) projects old forest per unit and schedule against the table percentages, with D.1-D.4 handled as stated in docs/forestry-old-forest.md.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of CFLB retained as old forest for units D1 to D7 (12-29%).
sections.gapNote: Transcribed in packages/legal-rules/rules/bc/prince-george/2004-biodiversity-order.json; values checked equal to the order here.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of CFLB retained as old forest for units E1 to E17 (12-58%).
sections.gapNote: Transcribed in the order JSON; values match. The printed E4 row ends with a stray comma ("SBS mk1, SBS wk3,"), kept as printed.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of CFLB retained as old forest for units A1 to A25 (12-84%); A3 is printed "combined with A13".
sections.gapNote: Transcribed in the order JSON; values match, including A10 at 17% (DataBC's OLD_RETEN of 0.12 is reported, not used). Printed typos kept: A2 "EESF wc3", A5 lists "ESSF mv3" twice.

sections.bearsOn: A percentage of the old forest required under objective A must be old interior forest, per Tables 4 to 6 and subject to section D.
sections.gapNote: Interior is computed by the 2005 buffering method by default (2004 on request); the denominator is the required old forest, not the CFLB, as the order JSON records.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of the required old forest that must be old interior forest for D1 to D7 (10-40%).
sections.gapNote: Transcribed; values match.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of required old forest that must be interior for E1 to E17 (10-40%).
sections.gapNote: Transcribed; values match.

sections.bearsOn: Sets the minimum percent of required old forest that must be interior for A1 to A25 (10-40%).
sections.gapNote: Transcribed; values match.

sections.bearsOn: Licensees must demonstrate a trend toward the Table 7 young forest patch size distribution by natural disturbance sub-unit within each forest district; a block's size and placement changes the patches.
sections.gapNote: The patch analysis (spatial/patch-analysis.json, pg-2005-buffer-v1) computes the distribution; the trend rule flags any class that moved farther from its target. That is stricter than the text, which asks for a trend toward the distribution as a whole: a reviewer may see a flag while the overall distance shrinks.

sections.bearsOn: Gives each natural disturbance sub-unit's target share of young forest in patches >1000, 101-1000, 51-100 and <50 ha.
sections.gapNote: Targets transcribed and match. The printed classes leave patches of 50-51 ha unassigned ("<50" and "51 - 100"); the JSON flags the 50 ha boundary for review. Table 7 names "Omineca - Valley" where Tables 2 and 5 say "Omineca - low elevation".

sections.bearsOn: OGMAs established before the order continue, and the entire area of OGMAs and of new spatially located old forest retention areas counts toward objectives A and B; parks and protected areas may count.
sections.gapNote: Code counts legal OGMAs whole, non-legal OGMAs (which now hold the PG district COFAs) by default, and parks by switch. The 2022 letter of expectations counts only the old forest inside OGMAs, parks, UWRs, WHAs and WTRAs, so its net targets will not match the planner's figures; the code follows the order's "entire area".

sections.bearsOn: A licensee with similar mBECs in several forest districts may meet the old and old interior requirements over their combined area.
sections.gapNote: pooling.ts pools only units the reviewer names; each unit is calculated alone and summed.

sections.bearsOn: Affected stands may contribute a representative portion, and licensees must ensure a representative portion of unaffected (non-pine) stands is used to meet objectives A and B.
sections.gapNote: Code sets non-pine old forest against policy Tables 8-10 and prints a representation summary; whether old forest is representative stays the reviewer's judgement. The affected-stands rule only asks for evidence, although the second sentence is a "must".

sections.bearsOn: Up to 20% of the old forest and old interior objectives may be younger age classes where equal or better conservation benefits are demonstrated.
sections.gapNote: youngerStands.ts caps D.4 at 20% of each requirement, off by default, and needs the reviewer's age and conservation-benefit statement.

sections.bearsOn: Where old or old interior objectives cannot be achieved, considering timely and economic harvesting, a recruitment strategy must be submitted, approved by the minister's designate and complied with.
sections.gapNote: The determination is the reviewer's; the planner shows its A/B result beside it. The 2022 letter says mBECs inside COFAs need no recruitment strategy and that A04 runs under an approved 2012 spatial recruitment strategy; the rule does not know either.

sections.bearsOn: Where the young patch size objective cannot be achieved, a rationale with results or strategies reaching the objective in the shortest practicable time must be submitted.
The order does not affect Category A cutblocks approved under the FPC on or before 20 October 2004.
sections.gapNote: The transition rule asks one generic question about pre-existing approvals; nothing asks whether the block is a pre-order Category A cutblock. Rare today.
